title: Windsurf Pricing: Plans, Limits & Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Windsurf pricing for the Pro plan is $20 monthly as of 2026, up from $15, with charges based on usage rather than unlimited.
body_markdown:
## Tracking AI Tool Spend with Activepieces


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) runs as a per-project MCP server, so Windsurf can build the spend-tracking flow itself: it creates the flow, edits it when an invoice format changes, and explains what each step does, all from inside the editor and without a separate builder UI.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production, and Activepieces keeps run history for the flow once it is running, and audit logs (Enterprise Edition) record activity across projects. The flow only watches the bill; it doesn't change what Windsurf charges.


That distinction matters because the problem here's scattered data. Each tool meters something different: Windsurf meters usage against a quota, another vendor meters seats, a third meters tokens.


Each sends its own invoice to a different inbox. Nobody sees the combined total until someone builds it by hand, and by then the month is closed.


Below, invoices and seat lists from several AI tools flow into one scheduled Activepieces flow, built from a library of 746 integrations in the open source monorepo, meaning you probably don't have to build custom integrations for your tools, which outputs a single summary to a Slack channel and a spreadsheet, letting you monitor all your AI subscriptions from a single view.


The workflow is a collector. It puts the quota-driven charges next to the seat charges so a team can see which line is growing.


### What an AI tool spend-check workflow does


On a schedule you set, the flow pulls the latest invoice and seat count from each tool, adds them up, and writes one row per tool to a sheet. It then posts a short message to a Slack channel.


It's the row history that's useful. When a Windsurf line climbs while the seat count stays flat, the quota's driving the bill, which is the pattern this article has been tracing.


A weekly check across a handful of tools is a small, predictable unit: an Activepieces run is 1 credit however many steps it has, and the free plan includes 1,000 credits a month, so a weekly schedule uses about four or five of them.


AI steps inside the flow cost more than that, so count those separately.


### When a spend-tracking workflow isn't worth building


For a solo developer on one Windsurf plan, there's one invoice and one dashboard, and a workflow adds a tool to maintain without adding visibility. The same holds for a small team with a single vendor: the vendor's own usage page already shows the number.


Only when several seats are spread across several tools, and no one person already opens all of those invoices, does the flow earn its setup time.
